subject: Urgent: Checkoutly p99 surge & parsing failures - possible client protocol mismatch
messages:
From: Lisa Grant <lisa@checkoutly.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marco.ruiz@checkoutly.com, node-monitoring@checkoutly.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Increasing p99 & stream parse errors on checkout endpoints

Hey Aisha,

We started seeing a sharp p99 latency increase and a spike in 5xxs for the /v1/live-checkout stream between 08:45 and 09:05 PDT. Our monitoring flagged repeated parser failures in the client logs: "incomplete header block / trailer missing" and a bunch of truncated JSON payloads. Attach I included a small packet dump and the monitoring alert.

This is impacting a subset of our high-value customers — conversion dropped ~6% during the window. Can your team triage? We rolled back to an earlier client SDK yesterday (v1.6.2 -> v1.5.9) but the issue persisted.

We need:
- Quick mitigation (fallback to non-streaming endpoint or increased retries)
- A timeline for root cause
- Any temporary config changes we should apply on our side

Thanks,
Lisa
---
Lisa Grant
Head of Integrations, Checkoutly
---
Attachments: packet_dump_20260503.log (text), slo_summary_may3.pdf (pdf)
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Lisa Grant <lisa@checkoutly.com>, marco.ruiz@checkoutly.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing p99 & stream parse errors on checkout endpoints

Thanks for the heads-up, Lisa — sorry you’re hitting this. I’m looping in Rishi (on-call infra) and Vanessa (client integrations) to triage.

Immediate plan:
- Rishi: we can flip Checkoutly to the non-streaming fallback route and enable a short-term aggressive retry/backoff for the next 2 hours. Would you like us to make that change or do you prefer the toggle on your side?
- Vanessa: please review the packet dump and confirm whether the pattern looks like a server-side chunk/trailer loss or a client dechunking issue.

We’ll prioritize a rapid mitigation and come back with a root-cause hypothesis within 90 minutes.

Aisha
Product Lead, Integrations
Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Grant <lisa@checkoutly.com>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing p99 & stream parse errors on checkout endpoints

Quick triage notes after initial packet + infra logs:
- At ~08:46 we saw intermittent connection resets from edge-proxy -> upstream (AWS NLB) during bursts. Reset pattern correlated with heavy concurrent streams from Checkoutly.
- Packet dump shows some chunked-transfer payloads where the final chunk-trailer label is absent. Downstream client-side parser (Checkoutly SDK) reports "trailer missing" and drops the entire event.
- Our serving runtime did not emit errors; it appears we closed connections normally. There are traces where the final TCP FIN arrives but the proxy sends a reset before all bytes drained — possibly a keepalive/timeout interaction under high connection churn.

Short-term mitigation suggested (we can implement immediately):
1) Route Checkoutly to the non-streaming REST endpoint for 3 hours (this avoids chunked transfer and dechunking edge-cases).
2) Add an edge-proxy setting to wait 250ms before RST on idle drain for connections marked as streaming-heavy (default is 50ms).

Vanessa, can you confirm whether the SDK tolerates delayed FINs? If not, we should tell Checkoutly to switch to REST fallback and we’ll keep the streaming route off until we patch the proxy drain behavior.

Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Lisa Grant <lisa@checkoutly.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing p99 & stream parse errors on checkout endpoints

Thanks Rishi — looked through the packet dump and the SDK logs Lisa shared. Observations:
- The Checkoutly SDK (v1.6.2) appears to aggressively parse chunk boundaries and will discard an event if the trailer token is missing or if the chunked header and bytes don't align exactly. There is no graceful recovery path in the dechunker: once one event is discarded it restarts the parser state machine and may lose subsequent events until a full reconnect.
- We’ve seen variants of this before when proxy drains generate a RST during socket close. The SDK should be resilient, but this particular version lacks the tolerant dechunker found in our newer internal branch (we fixed a similar case in our internal 1.7.x branch).

Immediate steps I recommend:
- Aisha: ask Checkoutly to switch to REST fallback for now (my vote).
- I will prepare a targeted SDK patch (backport tolerant dechunker + handshake health-check) and provide a hotfix build (v1.6.3-hotfix) in ~4 hours.
- Rishi: apply the proxy drain wait-of-250ms change as a safety net.

I’ll attach a short repro and the minimal patch diff in the drive link.

Vanessa
Senior Integration Engineer
From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: Lisa Grant <lisa@checkoutly.com>, marco.ruiz@checkoutly.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 3 May 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Increasing p99 & stream parse errors on checkout endpoints

Lisa / Marco — quick update and ask for approval:

Summary so far:
- Root cause hypothesis: aggressive proxy RST/drain during connection close + a non-tolerant dechunker in Checkoutly SDK v1.6.2 causes truncated events to be dropped; high concurrency amplified the effect causing p99 spikes and error-rate increases.
- Short-term mitigations in flight: routing Checkoutly to REST fallback (avoids chunked dechunking), edge-proxy drain wait extended to 250ms, and Vanessa is building a hotfix SDK (v1.6.3-hotfix) that backports a tolerant dechunker.
- Expected timeline: REST fallback live within 15 minutes after you sign off; proxy change within 30–60 minutes; SDK hotfix + test artifacts in ~4 hours.

Ask: please confirm you want Redwood to flip Checkoutly to REST fallback from our side. If yes, we’ll proceed and send you a rollback window and a postmortem within 48 hours. If you prefer to toggle from your side, confirm when you’ll cutover.

If this affects your renewal / SLA concerns, Marissa (copied) is available to discuss credits and the commercial impact.

Thanks — will keep you posted on each action.

Aisha
Product Lead, Integrations
Redwood Inference
